Load a bundled simtte example mrgsolve model

Source: R/examples.R
simtte_example_model.Rd

Compiles (or loads from cache) one of simtte's shipped example mechanistic mrgsolve models; see simtte_example_models for the list of available names and what each model represents. This is a thin wrapper around mread_cache pointed at the package's example-model directory; it adds nothing beyond discoverability and an informative error for an unrecognized name.

Usage

simtte_example_model(name, ...)

Arguments

name

Character scalar naming one bundled model; must be an element of simtte_example_models().

...

Additional arguments passed to mread_cache (for example quiet = TRUE).

Value

A compiled mrgsolve model object.

Details

The returned model is a standard mrgsolve model object: use mrgsim to simulate it, exactly as with any other mrgsolve model. The underlying .cpp source file can be found under system.file("models", "examples", package = "simtte") and copied out and modified freely with any mrgsolve tooling; loading it through this function does not require continuing to use this function afterward.

Intended workflow

These example models are for use with sim_tte_df, the package's entry point for custom/mechanistic models with an ODE-integrated survival compartment (see its "Trajectory contract" section); they are not used by, and cannot be passed to, sim_tte, which only ever simulates its own built-in Weibull and M-spline models.


mod  <- simtte_example_model("pkpd_linear_hazard")
data <- mrgsolve::ev(amt = 100, cmt = 1, time = 0)
out  <- as.data.frame(mrgsolve::mrgsim(mod, data = data, end = -1,
          add = seq(0, 60, by = 0.5), obsonly = TRUE))
sim_tte_df(out[, c("ID", "time", "p11")])

See also

simtte_example_models, to list available names; sim_tte_df, which turns this model's simulated trajectory into event times. To simulate a model of your own with sim_tte_ode, convert it with tte_model.

Examples

# \donttest{
mod <- simtte_example_model("pkpd_linear_hazard")
#> Building pkpd_linear_hazard ... 
#> done.
# }
